record.paper_title: Pole solutions in the case of problems of flame front propagation and Saffman-Teylor "finger" formation without surface tension: open problems and possible ways of their solutions
record.context_brief: Velocity saturation in cylindrical flame-front propagation
record.original_question: For cylindrical flame-front propagation governed by the flame-front motion equation in the absence of explicit external noise, with only numerical noise present in simulations, does the flame-front velocity eventually saturate, or does it continue to accelerate indefinitely?

evidence.quote: For a cylindrical case of the flame front propagation problem at absence of noise (only numerical noise) (look [7] and the bibliography there) by Sivashinsky with help of numerical methods it was shown, that the flame front is continuously accelerated. During all this account time it is not visible any attributes of saturation. To increase time of the account is a difficult task. Hence, absence or presence of velocity saturation in a cylindrical case, as consequence of the flame front motion equation it is still a open problem yet.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Sivashinsky-type flame-front evolution equation governing the propagation of an outward-expanding cylindrical premixed flame front in two dimensions. Let the flame front be parameterized in polar form, and let its mean radial velocity (relative to the unburnt gas) be denoted V(t). Assume the dynamics are deterministic: no explicit stochastic external forcing is added to the equation, and the only perturbations present are those introduced by inevitable round-off and discretization errors in a numerical simulation.

Numerical evidence indicates that during all accessible computation times the mean flame-front velocity V(t) continuously increases, with no observable approach to a constant limit. The question is to determine the long-time behaviour of V(t) as t → ∞: does V(t) saturate to a finite limit (so that lim sup V(t) < ∞), or does V(t) grow without bound (i.e., accelerate indefinitely)? Provide a rigorous answer based solely on the deterministic flame-front motion equation in the cylindrical geometry.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on the Sivashinsky equation for outward (cylindrical/spherical) expanding flames continues to discuss self-similar acceleration and possible saturation regimes, but the question of whether the deterministic cylindrical Sivashinsky dynamics (without external noise) exhibit eventual velocity saturation or unbounded acceleration is still treated as unresolved; numerical simulations show ongoing acceleration with no observed saturation, and analytical proofs in either direction have not appeared.

status_evidence.title: Characteristics of cylindrical flame acceleration in outward expansion
status_evidence.snippet: Examines acceleration characteristics of outward-propagating cylindrical flames; observed acceleration regimes without clear saturation in the Sivashinsky framework.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical studies of cylindrical Sivashinsky-type dynamics report continuous acceleration without demonstrated saturation.

status_evidence.title: On transition to self-similar acceleration of spherically expanding flames with cellular instabilities
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses self-similar acceleration of expanding flames with cellular instabilities; saturation of cellular spectrum studied but long-time velocity behaviour remains under investigation.
status_evidence.claim: The long-time velocity behaviour of expanding-flame Sivashinsky dynamics is still an active topic without a definitive saturation result.
